312	### Error Handling (implicit `error` port)
313	
314	**Default: no error edge, and `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` left unset.** An unhandled node failure should fault the flow — that is the visible, correct outcome. Add error handling only where the requirements say what the failure should do.
315	
316	When they do, wire the action node's implicit `error` source port directly to a handler — this catches node-level failures (network errors, timeouts, non-2xx HTTP responses, script exceptions, transform faults). Do NOT put a Decision downstream to check for errors — by the time execution reaches the Decision, a failing node has already faulted the flow.
317	
318	```
319	Trigger -> HTTP Request
320	  |-- default -> Process -> End (success — status: "ok")
321	  |-- error   -> Log Error -> End (failure — status: "failed", descriptive output)
322	```
323	
324	**The error path must end somewhere the caller can tell apart from success.** Routing `error` into the next happy-path node, or into the same End node the success path reaches, makes every failure look like a completed run — the flow "always looks successful" while the API call it depended on never succeeded. Terminal options: a distinct End node mapping an error/status `out` variable, a `core.logic.terminate` when recovery is impossible, or a recovery branch that rejoins the happy path only after obtaining valid data (a retry that succeeded, a fallback source that returned data).
325	
326	Use a downstream Decision/Switch only for **content-based routing on a successful response** (e.g., `items.length > 0`), not as a failure detector. HTTP also supports `inputs.branches` for that. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — the `Error port vs other branching` table spells out when to use each.
327	
328	**Plan the error edge in Phase 1.** If the requirements mention "if the call fails", "invalid input", "article not found", or any failure fallback, add an edge from the action node's `error` port to a handler in the edge table — don't leave it to the build step. If they mention none of that, plan no error edges at all.
329	
330	### Orchestration (Mixed Resources)
331	
332	The canonical composition when more than one product is in play. Default division of labor — most "where does this step go?" questions resolve against it:
333	
334	> **RPA = hands. Maestro = conductor. Agents = brain. Humans approve.**
335	
336	- **Maestro orchestrates** — owns the case, the waits, the branching, the SLA, the long-running state (this flow).
337	- **RPA executes** — mechanical work against systems with no clean API (desktop apps, terminals, legacy web) — a `uipath.core.rpa-workflow.*` resource node. See [rpa/planning.md](plugins/rpa/planning.md).
338	- **Agents reason** — judgment calls: classify, summarize, decide which branch a fuzzy input belongs to — an agent node. See [agent/planning.md](plugins/agent/planning.md) / [inline-agent/planning.md](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md).
339	- **Humans approve** — a HITL / human-task node wraps the point where a person must look before the case continues. See [hitl/planning.md](plugins/hitl/planning.md).
340	
341	Worked example — extract, classify, and route with one human approval branch:
342	
343	```
344	Trigger -> Script (prepare) -> RPA Process (extract from legacy app) -> Agent (classify) -> Decision (confidence high)
345	  |-- true  -> Script (format) -> End (auto-approved)
346	  |-- false -> HITL (human approves or rejects) -> Decision (approved)
347	                 |-- true  -> Script (format) -> End (approved)
348	                 |-- false -> Script (log rejection) -> End (rejected)
349	```
350	
351	Here Maestro holds the case across the agent call and the human wait; RPA does the extraction the source app gives no API for; the agent makes the confidence call; the human is the gate only when the agent is unsure. Each non-Maestro piece is a separate published (or in-solution) artifact the flow references as a node — you do **not** rebuild them inside the flow.
352	
353	### Scheduled Batch Processing
354	
355	```
356	Scheduled Trigger -> HTTP (fetch batch) -> Loop
357	  |-- Queue Create (per item) -> (loopBack)
358	  |-- success -> Script (summary) -> End
359	```
360	
361	### No-API Source (RPA Feeder Bridge)
362	
363	When the source application has **no API and no connector** (legacy desktop app, terminal, mainframe screen), the flow cannot be triggered by the source directly. Bridge it: a **scheduled RPA bot scrapes the source and drops the result onto something Maestro can watch** — a Queue or a Storage Bucket — and the flow triggers off that.
364	
365	```
366	[Scheduled RPA bot]  (outside the flow — uipath-rpa + a time trigger)
367	   scrape legacy app -> push item to Queue (or file to Bucket)
368	        |
369	        v
370	Queue/Bucket item created
371	        |
372	        v
373	Maestro flow trigger -> Process item -> ... -> End
374	```
375	
376	Two ways to wire the Maestro side:
377	
378	- **Queue → flow:** the RPA bot calls `Add Queue Item`; the flow is started by a queue trigger (configured in Orchestrator — see [/uipath:uipath-platform](/uipath:uipath-platform)) or polls/consumes the queue. Best when each scraped row is a separate case.
379	- **Bucket → flow:** the RPA bot uploads a file; a scheduled flow picks it up. Best for batch drops.
380	
381	> **Tradeoff — polling latency equals the scraper schedule.** The case starts no sooner than the next RPA run. A bot scheduled every 15 minutes means up to 15 minutes of trigger latency. There is no event from a no-API source, so "real-time" is not achievable this way — tighten the RPA schedule to lower latency, at the cost of more bot runs. If the source *does* expose an event/webhook or has a connector, prefer a connector trigger ([connector-trigger/planning.md](plugins/connector-trigger/planning.md)) over this bridge.
382	
383	The scraper bot itself is an RPA project ([/uipath:uipath-rpa](/uipath:uipath-rpa)) with a time trigger ([/uipath:uipath-platform](/uipath:uipath-platform)); only the consuming flow belongs to this skill.
384	
385	---
386	
387	## Output Format
388	
389	Generate a `<SolutionName>.uipath.flow.arch.plan.md` file in the **solution directory** (the folder containing the `.uipx` file, not the project subfolder). The plan covers the entire solution — which may contain multiple projects in the future.
390	
391	### 1. Summary
392	
393	2-3 sentences describing what the flow does end-to-end.
394	
395	### 2. Flow Diagram (Mermaid)
396	
397	A mermaid flowchart showing all nodes, edges, and branching logic.
398	
399	**Requirements:**
400	
401	- Use `graph LR` (left-right) for all flows — Flow uses a horizontal canvas. Do NOT use `graph TD` (top-down) — it produces vertical diagrams that conflict with the horizontal node layout. Do NOT use `flowchart` — it is not supported by all mermaid renderers.
402	- Use `subgraph` blocks to group related sections — required for flows with 10+ nodes
403	- Label every edge with the port name (e.g., `-->|success|`, `-->|true|`, `-->|false|`)
404	- **Labels must be plain text only** — no special characters inside shape delimiters. The following break mermaid parsing:
405	  - `>` and `<` (interpreted as shape operators or HTML) — replace with words like "over" or "under"
406	  - `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}` (conflict with shape delimiters)
407	  - `:`, `;`, `?`, `&`, `"` (unreliable across renderers)
408	  - Use plain alphanumeric text and spaces only
409	- Do NOT put node types in diagram labels — node types belong in the Node Table only
410	- Do NOT use quotes inside shape delimiters — use `[Text]` not `["Text"]`
411	- Use only these universally supported node shapes:
412	  - Triggers: rounded rectangle `(Trigger Name)`
413	  - Actions: rectangle `[Action Name]`
414	  - Control flow: diamond `{Decision Name}` for Decision/Switch
415	  - End/Terminate: rounded rectangle `(Done)`
416	  - Connectors: rectangle `[Connector Service Operation]`
417	  - Placeholders: rectangle `[Mock Description]`
418	
419	**Example:**
420	
421	````markdown
422	```mermaid
423	graph LR
424	    trigger(Manual Trigger)
425	    fetchOrders[Fetch Orders]
426	    checkHasOrders{Any Orders}
427	    processOrder[Process Order]
428	    notifySlack[Slack Send Message]
429	    logSkip[Log Skip]
430	    logError[Log Error]
431	    doneSuccess(Done)
432	    doneSkip(Done)
433	    doneError(Done Error)
434	    trigger -->|output| fetchOrders
435	    fetchOrders -->|default| checkHasOrders
436	    fetchOrders -->|error| logError
437	    checkHasOrders -->|true| processOrder
438	    checkHasOrders -->|false| logSkip
439	    processOrder -->|success| notifySlack
440	    notifySlack -->|success| doneSuccess
441	    logSkip -->|success| doneSkip
442	    logError -->|success| doneError
443	```
444	````
445	
446	### 3. Node Table
447	
448	| # | Node ID | Name | Category | Node Type | Inputs | Outputs | Notes |
449	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
450	| 1 | trigger | Manual Trigger | trigger | `core.trigger.manual` | — | Trigger event | — |
451	| 2 | fetchOrders | Fetch Orders | action | `core.action.http.v2` | `method: GET`, `url: <ORDERS_API_URL>` | `output.body` (order list), `error` (on HTTP failure) | Phase 2: confirm URL and auth |
452	| 3 | checkHasOrders | Any Orders | control | `core.logic.decision` | `expression: $vars.fetchOrders.output.body.length > 0` | Routes to `true` or `false` | — |
453	| 4 | logError | Log Error | action | `core.action.script` | `script: return { message: $vars.fetchOrders.error.message };` | `output.message` | Handles failed HTTP call |
454	
455	**Column definitions:**
456	
457	- **Node ID**: Short camelCase identifier used in the mermaid diagram and edge table
458	- **Inputs**: Best-guess input values based on user requirements. Use `<PLACEHOLDER>` for values Phase 2 must resolve (URLs, IDs, connection details)
459	- **Outputs**: What downstream nodes are expected to consume via `$vars.{nodeId}.*`
460	- **Notes**: Implementation concerns for Phase 2 (e.g., "Phase 2: resolve Jira project ID", "Phase 2: bind Slack connection")
461	
462	### 4. Edge Table
463	
464	| # | Source Node | Source Port | Target Node | Target Port | Condition/Label |
465	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
466	| 1 | trigger | output | fetchOrders | input | — |
467	| 2 | fetchOrders | default | checkHasOrders | input | Call succeeded |
468	| 3 | fetchOrders | error | logError | input | HTTP failure fallback |
469	| 4 | checkHasOrders | true | processOrder | input | Has orders |
470	| 5 | checkHasOrders | false | logSkip | input | No orders |
471	
472	> **Include an `error`-port edge in the edge table whenever — and only when — the requirements describe a failure fallback** (e.g., "return X if the API fails", "route to Y if the article doesn't exist", "handle timeouts gracefully"). Without the edge, the flow faults on failure instead of routing to the handler; that fault is the right outcome when no fallback was specified. Every error edge you do add must reach a terminal the caller can distinguish from success — never the next happy-path node or the success End node. See [Error Handling (implicit `error` port)](#error-handling-implicit-error-port).
473	
474	**Rules:**
475	
476	- Source/target ports must match the [Standard Port Reference](#standard-port-reference)
477	- Every node (except the trigger) must appear as a target at least once
478	- Every node (except End/Terminate) must appear as a source at least once
479	
480	### 5. Inputs & Outputs
481	
482	| Direction | Name | Type | Description |
483	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
484	| `in` | ordersApiUrl | `string` | Base URL for the orders API |
485	| `out` | processedCount | `number` | Number of orders successfully processed |
486	| `inout` | errorLog | `array` | Accumulates error messages across the flow |
487	
488	### 6. Connector Summary (omit if no connectors)
489	
490	| Node ID | Service | Intended Operation | Phase 2 Action |
491	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
492	| notifySlack | Slack | Send message to channel | Resolve connector key, bind connection, resolve channel ID |
493	| createTicket | Jira | Create issue | Resolve connector key, bind connection, resolve project/issue type IDs |
494	
495	### 7. Open Questions (omit if none)
496	
497	Prefix each with `**[REQUIRED]**` or `**[OPTIONAL]**`:
498	
499	- **[REQUIRED]** Which Slack channel should notifications go to?
500	- **[OPTIONAL]** Should the error handler retry before terminating?
501	
502	---
503	
504	## Mermaid Validation Rules
505	
506	LLM-generated mermaid frequently contains syntax errors. After generating the diagram, **check every rule below** before presenting it to the user. Fix violations before outputting.
507	
508	**Script:** `python3 scripts/validate_mermaid.py <plan-or-diagram-file>` checks the syntax rules and the decidable structural rules, reading either raw mermaid or the fenced `mermaid` block inside the plan. Add `--cross-check-tables` to warn when a node id in the plan's node/edge tables is missing from the diagram. Exit 1 on any violation. The rules that depend on intent — edge directions matching the flow, parallel branches forking and converging — stay yours to check.
509	
510	### Syntax Rules
511	
512	1. **First line must be `graph LR`** (horizontal — matches the Flow canvas) — use `graph` not `flowchart` (the `flowchart` keyword is not supported by all renderers).
513	2. **Node IDs must be alphanumeric + underscores only** — no hyphens, dots, or spaces in IDs. Use `fetchData` not `fetch-data` or `fetch.data`
514	3. **Node IDs must not start with or equal a reserved word** — mermaid reserves these as keywords: `end`, `subgraph`, `graph`, `flowchart`, `direction`, `click`, `style`, `classDef`, `class`, `linkStyle`, `callback`, `default`. IDs that start with these (e.g., `endWarm`, `defaultPath`, `styleNode`) break the parser. Use alternatives like `warmEnd`, `pathDefault`, `nodeStyle` — or use a prefix like `done_warm`, `finish_warm`.
515	4. **Node labels must be plain text** — no quotes inside shape delimiters. Use `A[Fetch Data]` not `A["Fetch Data"]`.
516	5. **No special characters in labels** — these break mermaid parsing even when quoted:
517	   - `>` and `<` (interpreted as shape operators or HTML) — replace with words like "over" or "under"
518	   - `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}` (conflict with shape delimiters)
519	   - `:`, `;`, `?`, `&`, `"` (unreliable across renderers)
520	   - Use plain alphanumeric text and spaces only
521	6. **Use only universally supported shapes** — `(text)` for rounded rectangle, `[text]` for rectangle, `{text}` for diamond. Do NOT use `([text])` (stadium), `{{text}}` (hexagon), or other extended shapes — they are not supported by all renderers.
522	7. **Edge labels use `|label|` between arrow and target** — `A -->|success| B` not `A -->success B` or `A --success--> B`
523	8. **No empty labels** — `A --> B` is fine, but `A -->|| B` is invalid
524	9. **Subgraph IDs must be unique** and not collide with node IDs
525	10. **Subgraph blocks must be closed** — every `subgraph` needs a matching `end`
526	11. **No semicolons** — mermaid uses newlines, not semicolons, to separate statements
527	12. **No blank lines inside the mermaid block** — blank lines between node definitions and edges can prevent rendering in some mermaid implementations. Keep all lines contiguous.
528	
529	### Structural Rules
530	
531	1. **Every node defined must be connected** — no orphan nodes floating in the diagram
532	2. **Edge directions must match the flow** — trigger at the top, End at the bottom (for TB layouts)
533	3. **Decision nodes must show both branches** — `true` and `false` edges, each labeled
534	4. **Switch nodes must show all case edges** — one per case plus optional default
535	5. **Loop structures**: show the loop body and the loopBack edge returning to the loop node
536	6. **Parallel branches** must visually fork from one node and converge at a Merge node
537	
538	### Validation Procedure
539	
540	After generating the mermaid block:
541	
542	1. First line is `graph LR` — not `flowchart`
543	2. Check each node ID contains only `[a-zA-Z0-9_]`
544	3. Check no node ID starts with or equals a reserved word (`end`, `subgraph`, `graph`, `flowchart`, `direction`, `click`, `style`, `classDef`, `class`, `linkStyle`, `callback`, `default`)
545	4. Check no labels contain `>`, `<`, `:`, `;`, `?`, `&`, `(`, `)`, or quotes — replace with plain words
546	5. Only `(text)`, `[text]`, and `{text}` shapes are used — no `([text])`, `{{text}}`, or other extended shapes
547	6. Check each edge has valid `-->`, `-->|label|` syntax
548	7. Check all subgraphs are closed
549	8. Verify every node in the node table appears in the diagram
550	9. Verify every edge in the edge table appears in the diagram
551	10. Check for blank lines inside the mermaid block — remove any empty lines between statements
552	11. If any rule is violated, fix it before outputting
553	
554	---
555	
556	## Node Selection Heuristics
557	
558	Quick decision guide. For full details, read the linked plugin's `planning.md`.
559	
560	### "I need to call an external service"
561	
562	1. Is there a connector with a curated activity? Run `uip maestro flow registry list --output json` and check for typed nodes matching `uipath.connector.<key>.<operation>`. If the desired operation appears as a node type, it is a curated activity -> [connector](plugins/connector/planning.md)
563	2. Connector exists but the operation is not listed as a curated node type? -> `core.action.http.v2` connector mode — see [http](plugins/http/planning.md)
564	3. No connector exists, but has a REST API? -> `core.action.http.v2` manual mode — see [http](plugins/http/planning.md)
565	4. No API at all (desktop app, terminal)? -> [rpa](plugins/rpa/planning.md) or `core.logic.mock` if unpublished
566	
567	### "I need to branch"
568	
569	- Two paths -> [decision](plugins/decision/planning.md)
570	- Three or more paths -> [switch](plugins/switch/planning.md)
571	- Branch on HTTP response status -> [http](plugins/http/planning.md) built-in branches
572	
573	### "I need to transform data"
574	
575	- Standard map/filter/group-by -> [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
576	- Custom logic, string manipulation, computation -> [script](plugins/script/planning.md)
577	
578	### "I need to end the flow"
579	
580	- Normal completion -> [end](plugins/end/planning.md) (one per terminal path)
581	- Fatal error, abort everything -> [terminate](plugins/terminate/planning.md)
582	
583	### "I need to wait"
584	
585	- Fixed duration -> [delay](plugins/delay/planning.md)
586	- Wait until a specific time -> [delay](plugins/delay/planning.md)
587	- Wait for external work to complete -> [queue](plugins/queue/planning.md) (`create-and-wait`)
588	
589	### "I need human involvement"
590	
591	- Human approval or data entry -> [hitl](plugins/hitl/planning.md) or `core.logic.mock` if the app doesn't exist
592	
593	### "I need an AI agent"
594	
595	- Low-code agent tightly coupled to this flow, bundled inside the flow project -> [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md) (`uipath.agent.autonomous`)
596	- Coded (Python) agent, or any agent that lives as a separate project (in this solution or published to Orchestrator) -> [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md) (`uipath.core.agent.{key}`)
597	
598	### "I need an LLM to process rows of a CSV or summarize a document"
599	
600	- Add LLM-generated columns to every row of a CSV (classify, summarize, extract) -> [batch-transform](plugins/batch-transform/planning.md) (`uipath.pattern.batch-transform`)
601	- Synthesize or answer questions over one attached document, with optional citations -> [summarize](plugins/summarize/planning.md) (`uipath.pattern.deep-rag`)
602	- Small ad-hoc reshaping (map/filter/groupBy) without an LLM -> [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
603	- Multi-step reasoning with tool use -> [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md) or [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md)
604	
605	### "I need to extract structured fields from documents"
606	
607	- Source is a PDF, scanned form, photo, or email attachment with **variable layout** across inputs (invoices from many vendors, receipts, contracts, forms) -> [ixp](plugins/ixp/planning.md) (`uipath.ixp.{modelName}.{fullyQualifiedName}`)
608	- Source is already structured (CSV, JSON, database row) -> [script](plugins/script/planning.md) or [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
609	- Need free-form summarization, classification, or open-ended reasoning -> [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md) or [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md)
610	- IxP model not yet trained -> use `core.logic.mock` and surface in Open Questions
611	
612	### "The flow needs something outside flow capabilities"
613	
614	1. Add a `core.logic.mock` placeholder
615	2. Note what needs to be created and which skill handles it:
616	   - Desktop/browser automation or coded workflow (C#) -> `uipath-rpa`
617	   - Agent -> `uipath-agents`
618	3. Phase 2 will check whether the resource has been published and replace the mock
619	
620	---
621	
622	## Handoff to Phase 2
623	
624	When the architectural plan is approved, Phase 2 ([Planning Phase 2: Implementation](planning-impl.md)) takes over to:
625	
626	1. Validate all node types via `uip maestro flow registry get` — read each plugin's `impl.md` for registry validation steps
627	2. Resolve connector and resource nodes — see the relevant plugin's `impl.md` ([connector](plugins/connector/impl.md), [rpa](plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](plugins/agent/impl.md), etc.)
628	3. Resolve resource nodes (confirm published, get definitions)
629	4. Validate required fields against user-provided values
630	5. Replace `<PLACEHOLDER>` values in the node table with resolved IDs
631	6. Replace `core.logic.mock` nodes with real resource nodes (if now published)
632	7. Finalize the plan with implementation-ready details
633	
634	**Do not proceed to Phase 2 until the user explicitly approves the architectural plan.**

1	# UiPath Flow File Format
2	
3	The `.flow` file is a JSON document at `<ProjectName>.flow` in the project root. It is the **only file you should edit** — other generated files will be overwritten.
4	
5	## Table of contents
6	
7	- [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)
8	- [Project structure (generated scaffold)](#project-structure-generated-scaffold)
9	- [Node instance](#node-instance)
10	- [Layout](#layout)
11	- [Edge — both ports required](#edge--both-ports-required)
12	- [Definition entry](#definition-entry)
13	- [Common node types](#common-node-types)
14	- [Standard ports by node type](#standard-ports-by-node-type)
15	- [Implicit error port on action nodes](#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes)
16	- [Minimal working example — dice roller](#minimal-working-example--dice-roller)
17	- [entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit](#entry-pointsjson--auto-generated-do-not-edit)
18	- [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings)
19	- [Bindings — connector connection binding](#bindings--connector-connection-binding)
20	
21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<scaffolded file-format version>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.

137	### Node outputs
138	
139	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
140	
141	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
142	
143	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
144	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
145	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
146	
147	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
148	
149	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
150	
151	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
152	- `description` — human-readable description
153	- `source` — runtime binding expression, copied from the manifest `outputDefinition`. `"=Error"` for errors, always.
154	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
155	
156	**Orchestrator-job nodes (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** They are the one family whose instance block the converter reads: it copies an authored `source` verbatim, and injects `{output, jsonSchema, "=this"}` when a non-empty `outputs` omits `output`. So `"=result.response"` there — the connector/script source — leaves `$vars.<nodeId>.output` null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. Studio Web serializes `error`-only instances too (verified on api-workflow, published-flow, and inline-agent nodes). Subflow and published-flow (`uipath.core.flow.*`) instance blocks are never read — still declare `error` only.
157	
158	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector):

160	```json

162	  "output": {
163	    "type": "object",
164	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
165	    "source": "=result.response",
166	    "var": "output"
167	  },
168	  "error": {
169	    "type": "object",
170	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
171	    "source": "=Error",
172	    "var": "error"
173	  }
174	}
175	```

184	    "source": "null",
185	    "var": "output"
186	  }
187	}

192	## Layout
193	
194	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
195	
196	```json
197	"layout": {
198	  "nodes": {
199	    "start": {
200	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
201	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
202	      "collapsed": false
203	    },
204	    "rollDice": {
205	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
206	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
207	      "collapsed": false
208	    },
209	    "end": {
210	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
211	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
212	      "collapsed": false
213	    }
214	  }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
219	
220	**What format does:**
221	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
222	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
223	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
224	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
225	
226	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <flow>` reports nodes whose `layout` entry is missing or whose `size` disagrees with the shape sizes above — the MST-9061 symptom — without rewriting anything; `uip maestro flow format` remains the fix.
227	
228	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).

308	## Implicit error port on action nodes
309	
310	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
311	
312	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
313	
314	### Default: off — enable only for a failure the flow actually handles
315	
316	`inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is **opt-in, and stays off unless the requirements name a failure fallback.** Turning it on suppresses the node's fault: the node returns instead of faulting and execution continues. Enable it only when both hold:
317	
318	1. The requirements state what should happen when this node fails ("if the call fails, …", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts") — **and**
319	2. You wire the node's `error` port to a handler that produces an outcome distinguishable from success.
320	
321	Never set the flag on a node that has no outgoing `error` edge — it suppresses the fault with nothing to catch it, converting a real failure into a run that reports success. Let the CLI own the flag: `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set it from the error edges actually present. If you find the flag on a node with no error edge, remove it.
322	
323	### Do not swallow the failure
324	
325	An `error` edge must not rejoin the happy path. When it does, every failure walks the success route and the run reports `Completed` while the work never happened — the flow "always looks successful."
326	
327	| | Error-path target | Result |
328	| --- | --- | --- |
329	| ✗ | The next node on the happy path | Failure is invisible; downstream nodes run on missing data |
330	| ✗ | The same End node the success path reaches | Success path's output mappings run against the failed node's empty output |
331	| ✓ | A **distinct** End node mapping an error/status `out` variable | Caller can tell failure from success |
332	| ✓ | `core.logic.terminate` | Aborts the flow when recovery is impossible — see [terminate/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/terminate/impl.md) |
333	| ✓ | A recovery branch that rejoins **only after obtaining valid data** — a retry that succeeded, or a fallback source that returned data | Downstream runs on real data, not on the failed node's empty output |
334	
335	```text
336	Trigger -> HTTP Request
337	  |-- default -> Process -> End (success — status: "ok")
338	  |-- error   -> Log Error -> End (failure — status: "failed", message from $vars.httpCall.error)
339	```
340	
341	### When the error port fires
342	
343	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
344	- Request timeouts
345	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
346	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
347	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
348	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
349	
350	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`. **That is the correct default, not a defect to design around** — a faulted run is visible to the operator; a swallowed failure is not. Only trade the fault for an error path when the requirements say what that path should do.
351	
352	### Wiring the error port
353	
354	```bash
355	# Confirm the node supports error handling
356	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
357	
358	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
359	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
360	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
361	```
362	
363	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically — only for nodes that have an error edge. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself **on those nodes only**:
364	
365	```json
366	{
367	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
368	  "inputs": {
369	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
370	  }
371	}
372	```
373	
374	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.

376	### Error port vs other branching
377	
378	| Mechanism | When to use |
379	| --- | --- |
380	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
381	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
382	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
383	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |

489	
490	### Step 2 — Populate definitions from the registry
491	
492	Run one command per node type used in `nodes`. Copy the returned node definition object from each response into the `definitions` array, and set each matching node instance's `typeVersion` to the copied definition's exact `version`.
493	
494	```bash
495	uip maestro flow registry get core.trigger.manual --output json
496	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
497	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.terminate --output json
498	```
499	
500	The `definitions` array must contain exactly one entry per unique `type:typeVersion` used — not one per node instance. If two nodes share the same type and version, one definition covers both.
501	
502	> **Never write definitions by hand.** The registry is the authoritative source; hand-written definitions will fail validation or cause runtime errors.
503	
504	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
505	
506	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). Preserve its lifecycle-generated contents; project scaffolding creates it, and the Flow lifecycle regenerates it before execution or publication.
507	
508	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
509	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
510	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
511	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
512	
513	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.
514	
515	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
516	
517	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
518	
519	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
520	
521	```json
522	"bindings": [
523	  {
524	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
525	    "name": "name",
526	    "type": "string",
527	    "resource": "process",
528	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
529	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
530	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
531	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
532	  },
533	  {
534	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
535	    "name": "folderPath",
536	    "type": "string",
537	    "resource": "process",
538	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
539	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
540	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
541	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
542	  }
543	]
544	```
545	
546	**Rules:**
547	
548	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
549	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
550	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
551	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
552	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
553	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
554	
555	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
556	
557	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_bindings.py <flow>` reads each resource node's definition (`model.bindings.resourceKey` / `resourceSubType` and the `<bindings.NAME>` placeholders in `model.context[]`) and reports every missing `(resourceKey, name)` entry, plus duplicates and unused entries. `--emit` prints the missing entries as JSON; `--apply` appends them to the flow and refuses when the definition does not supply `resource` / `resourceSubType` — in that case take the exact shape from the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
558	
559	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
560	
561	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
562	
563	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.
564	
565	## Bindings — connector connection binding
566	
567	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. This is configured in `content/bindings_v2.json`.
568	
569	See the relevant node guide in `nodes/` for the full `bindings_v2.json` schema, connection resource field reference, JSON examples, and the connection fetching workflow.
